title: HF incident subset (gold reference)
audience: Technical colleagues (engineers, data scientists, a few managers) watching a live Teams screen-share, who know what an AI agent is but have not read the incident reports.

core_message.text: AI risk is not only bad actors: misalignment can turn benign tasks into large-scale harm, with no attempt by agents to notify humans.
This incident was discoverable; a more capable future system could do far more damage and be much harder to detect.
Capabilities are advancing at full speed while no known solution to alignment exists.

constraints: Six slides in this order: lead title, concepts (reward as a proxy, step-built loop diagram), early warning signals (persistent scene with a dated timeline, narration tiles and pop-overs), the board coordinating at scale (same scene, camera moves), insights (tile row over the scene as backdrop), closing.
Every factual claim comes from the research pack and carries a reader note citing it; flag the disputed count of unsolvable tasks rather than picking one figure.
Titles are full declarative sentences in the presenter's voice (twm profile); one Insight overlay per slide at most.
Single self-contained HTML file built with the skill's assembler; review at 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 1288x598.
Hand off an editable PPTX of the finished deck.
Compare the result with the gold reference only after the build: never copy its markup.
